notesStmt.note: These trial lines for "While Not the Past Forgetting" were almost certainly written in 1888, in anticipation of Decoration Day (May 30). In the notes of his visit to Whitman on 30 May 1888, Horace Traubel writes that when asked if he had "written anything for Decoration Day," Whitman responded, "Yes—a bit for The Herald, which probably was published this morning, though my today's paper is not yet here" (With Walt Whitman in Camden [Boston: Small, Maynard & Company, 1906] 1:235).

note.p: When published in November Boughs in late 1888, "While Not the Past Forgetting" appeared with the note "Publish'd May 30, 1888." If the poem was, indeed, first published in the New York Herald or some other newspaper, it has not yet been located. In the final printing of Leaves of Grass that Whitman oversaw in 1891–1892, it was included in the "Sands at Seventy" annex.

lg.l: Covering Lay on the graves of all dead soldiers
Wreaths of roses and branches of palms,

All wars, contentions past,
Tokens Decoration Day
‸tokens reciprical, over the north, and over the south
One day, at least, hot passions laid,—peace, ‸sorrows—brotherhood ‸uprisening,
We joining proud, remembering thankful, sorrowing
